title: Variables
summary: Variables are containers that store data values. They have a name and hold information that can change during program execution. Different programming languages handle variables differently - some require explicit type declarations while others infer types automatically.

title: Loops
summary: Loops allow you to repeat a block of code multiple times. The main types are for loops (iterate a specific number of times or over a collection) and while loops (continue until a condition becomes false). Loop control statements like break and continue give you fine control over execution.

title: Functions
summary: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks. They can accept input parameters, process data, and return output values. Functions help organize code, reduce repetition, and make programs easier to understand and maintain.

title: Conditionals
summary: Conditionals allow programs to make decisions based on conditions. The if statement executes code when a condition is true, else handles the false case, and elif/else if chains multiple conditions. Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) can combine multiple conditions.
sample_questions: What's the difference between == and === in JavaScript?

title: Arrays and Lists
summary: Arrays and lists are data structures that store multiple values in a single variable. They allow indexed access to elements, can be iterated over, and support various operations like adding, removing, and searching for items. Different languages implement them differently.
sample_questions: What's the difference between push and pop methods?

title: Objects and Classes
summary: Objects are instances of classes that bundle data (properties) and behavior (methods) together. Classes serve as blueprints for creating objects. Object-oriented programming uses concepts like inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism to organize code.

title: Asynchronous Programming
summary: Asynchronous programming allows code to handle multiple operations without blocking. Concepts include promises, async/await syntax, callbacks, and event loops. This is essential for I/O operations, network requests, and creating responsive applications.

title: Error Handling
summary: Error handling manages unexpected situations that occur during program execution. Try-catch blocks catch exceptions, finally blocks run cleanup code, and throw statements raise errors. Proper error handling makes programs robust and prevents crashes.
sample_questions: What's the difference between try, catch, and finally blocks?
